Bird, Frank Webb and Fred White. These all ran extremely well and we finished easy winners with Mitcham second and Croydon narrowly beating Epsom for third place.

Duncan, the Oxford Blue, was running for Reading, and won the 100 yards race, beating Gray, and Wiley, of our own club. Alby Bird ran away from his field in the 880 yards, and with Frank Webb and L.

The 4 x 880 was won in good style by our boys, and Frank Webb ran a very sound "half" to give us a convincing lead. In the 1 Mile team race Mitcham turned out a stronger team than at the first meeting; but our lads, led home by Les Cohen, proved too strong for their opponents, and actually finished as follows : L.
However, by re-arranging the teams, and bringing Albert Bird, Frank Webb and Fred White into the sprint events, with those sprinters who were available, we were able to make a good show.

Lee and Frank Webb gained standard medals for beating 2 mins. 8 secs. The 2 Miles Walk saw Bill Treacher and Harry Churcher having a battle royal throughout and it was only down the straight that the former just forged to the front, and so won a very fine race.

Frank Webb (24) beat an old rival in Harry Shields (22) for second place. A good race was seen in the Mile and in the last lap a small knot of three runners moved away, and then ensued a hectic struggle down the finishing straight.

In the 880 yards which followed, Alby Bird showed fine form in gaining first place with Frank Webb also scoring. Again in the 220 yards our sprinters were unable to make any headway, but this was again nullified as our boys, Tom Carter, Arthur Allum and Tommy Morrell, ran well to win the 2 Miles.
The 4 x 880 yards saw a ding-dong battle between the "Mental Hospital" boys and our lads; and over the first leg Frank Webb was just beaten by Leadbeater.
Tommy Morrell, off 90 yards, also put in a spectacular finish and eventually King was placed third. Frank Webb, off 35 yards, ran well to finish a close fourth in what was quite a fast-run race.

Dick Michael was a close fourth and Frank Webb was the other finalist. For three recognised half-milers to figure in a sprint final does not say much for the quality of our sprinters; but perhaps the handicapper was kind to them!

We also had two field event handicaps and in the Shot Putt the winner was, yes! Frank Webb. He made good use of his 16ft. start to win with 37ft. 6in., with Bill Sutton 37ft. 1½in., and George Powell 36ft. 10½in.
When they reached the far corner, Smart led Cohen by a yard with Carter and Verney just behind, followed by Arthur Penny, Harry Shields, Jerman, Herbert, Ring, Taylor, Frank Webb and Lucas.
The 4 x 880 yards came next and with Mitcham putting their best man first against Frank Webb, the latter did well to finish about 20 yards behind his opponent.

Thus with three events to go the score was: Belgrave 27, Old Tiffinians 27, but as two of these were the High and Long Jump and, moreover, we had to field Frank Webb in the High Jump (in which he did well to gain third place) we were soon behind, as Charlie Jones could only get second place in the Long Jump.
The S.A.A.L. 4 x 440 yards was also down for decision and we had to ask Jarlett and Gray to turn out once more for the Club, together with Dick Michael and Frank Webb.
Dick Michael made a fine substitute, however, and he ran well to beat Flynn of T.V.H., while Frank Webb sportingly turned out and gained points by finishing 4th.
In the Club Shot Putt handicap, the winner was Frank Webb. Now I know how he gets the nickname of “Snaky,” and he did 37ft. 5½in. with 15ft. start.
In the Senior 100 yards Southgate proved too strong for us; but Alby Bird credited us with first place in the 880 yards, and Frank Webb ran a fine race, to gain third place in this event.

… he is working back to his best form by winning off 100 yards; while Tommy Morrell (160) ran well to gain second place. Frank Webb (170) was third. To Frank it would appear that the distance is immaterial, be it anything from 300 yards to 10 miles.…
In the opening rush black vests were well to the fore, but when the runners turned down Golf Lane, Frank Webb jumped to the lead to remind us that once he could show us the way round.
Bowers gained a double, winning the 100 yards and 220 yards, with Frank Simmons 4th. The 440 yards was an easy win for Frank Webb, with Tommy Morrell, taking up sprinting, 2nd.

Belgrave again came out best in the above match, Len Marchant proving how much he has improved by again beating George Morris, T.V.H., the indoor half-mile champion, by inches, in 2mins. 4/5 secs., Frank Webb running as well as ever to finished 3rd.
Our first runner was our track captain Frank Webb, and he did well to finish sixth with Nicholson, of Woodford Green A.C., leading the field.

In proposing Frank Webb as a Life Member, Harry Shields paid tribute to his untiring efforts both as a Track Captain and an athlete. Frank Webb, pining to get back to England, has strained his heel and so kept out of training for the time being. Jack Rutland's many friends will be pleased to hear he is now fully recovered from his illness and has passed his Artillery Clerk's course and has been posted to Wales.

Frank Webb, having left Ireland, had a few weeks at Grantham, then on to Mildenhall, where he also played football and sprained his ankle. At the same time the Sports Officer had called him up to know if he was THE famous Belgrave Harrier!
Frank Webb is now an L.A.C. and is "on tour" again. Having "done" Lincolnshire, he had a brief stay in Yorkshire, and is now in Worcestershire for re-grading.
